evals.prompt: Build a runnable HTML/CSS product-listing section with a filter sidebar, a wrapping action row, and a card collection. Reuse the same section in a 22rem panel and a 70rem page without changing its markup or using viewport breakpoints as a proxy for available space. Include long translated labels and cards with unequal text lengths. Explain which layout primitives you composed and why; exercise narrow and wide containers in the browser, preserving reading order and keyboard access.
evals.expected_output: A complete composable layout with content-driven reflow, an explanation of primitive selection and alternatives, and observed narrow/wide behavior rather than assumed responsiveness.
assertions: At a fixed viewport width, the section fits both its 22rem and 70rem containers without horizontal overflow.
The filter sidebar stacks with the main content in the 22rem container and sits alongside it in the 70rem container.
The action row wraps its controls onto additional lines when their combined widths exceed the available inline space.
Long translated labels remain fully readable without clipping or overlap in the 22rem container.
Unequal card text lengths remain fully visible without overlapping adjacent cards.
The narrow and wide instances use the same section markup apart from unique identifiers needed for accessible controls.
Changing container width leaves the section's DOM reading order unchanged.
Keyboard traversal reaches every interactive control in DOM order at both container widths.
The explanation identifies the layout relationship each chosen primitive controls.

evals.prompt: Make a runnable reproduction of this nested card-list problem and fix it: the outer column uses gap: 1.5rem, every child also has margin-block: 1.5rem, a nested flex row contains a 12rem thumbnail and text, and one card contains a very long unbroken URL. At a 20rem container width the spacing compounds to 4.5rem (two child margins plus the gap) and content pushes the page sideways. Give spacing a clear owner, retain intentional internal card spacing, and handle the URL and intrinsic sizing without hiding overflow or clipping content. Show the before/after behavior at narrow and wide widths and with enlarged text.
evals.expected_output: An evidenced diagnosis and corrected HTML/CSS with predictable nested spacing and readable content at constrained widths; the fix addresses margin ownership and intrinsic sizing rather than suppressing overflow.
assertions: The before view reproduces horizontal overflow at a 20rem container width.
The before view has 4.5rem of edge-to-edge space between adjacent cards, accounting for two 1.5rem margins and the 1.5rem gap.
The fixed view has 1.5rem of edge-to-edge space between adjacent cards at both 20rem and 32rem container widths, with text at both 100% and 150%.
The fixed view has no horizontal overflow at either 20rem or 32rem container widths, with text at both 100% and 150%.
The fixed view preserves the reproduction's intentional internal card spacing, measured between the same internal elements before and after the fix.
The entire unbroken URL remains visible through wrapping in the fixed 20rem view.
The thumbnail and text remain non-overlapping at a 20rem container width with text enlarged to 150%.
The fix does not rely on overflow hiding, clipping, or text truncation to make the content fit.
The explanation attributes the excess inter-card spacing to the additive child margins and parent gap.

evals.prompt: Use the Every Layout Center custom element in a runnable page with two independently configured instances. Inspect the website-linked Center download rather than inventing its API. Include its companion CSS and the tokens those styles need, set a measure and visible gutters, and explain why importing JavaScript alone is insufficient. Explain how the downloaded element reads attributes, registers, and generates CSS; compare the documented gutters type with the downloaded getter. Exercise initial rendering and a later attribute change, reporting what actually updates without silently rewriting the upstream lifecycle. Keep the DOM light and explain the CSS-only alternative. Do not republish the complete paid component sources.
evals.expected_output: A runnable, correctly styled light-DOM component example with explicit stylesheet/token dependencies, source-grounded API and lifecycle explanation, the documented/downloaded gutters distinction, and honest observed configuration behavior.
assertions: The rendered Center instances retain their authored children in the light DOM.
At a width with spare inline space, each Center instance has balanced outer inline margins.
Each instance's rendered content width respects its independently configured maximum measure.
Each instance's rendered inline padding matches its configured CSS gutters value.
Changing the first instance's max attribute to 40ch after connection updates its rendered content-width cap without a page reload.
Changing the first instance's gutters attribute to 1rem after connection updates its rendered inline padding without a page reload.
Changing the first instance's attributes leaves the second instance's rendered width and gutters unchanged.
The explanation distinguishes the documented boolean gutters type from the downloaded getter's CSS string value.
The explanation identifies the block display, content-box sizing, and auto margins supplied by companion CSS rather than JavaScript.
The explanation identifies the token definitions required by the included companion styles.
The lifecycle explanation describes attribute-backed getters, center-l registration, and configuration-scoped generated CSS consistently with the inspected download.
The CSS-only alternative preserves bounded measure, balanced outer margins, and narrow-width gutters without custom-element JavaScript.
The delivered example does not reproduce the complete paid component sources.
